sections.content: You know *en resumen* and *en definitiva* from B2 Unit 28: they close a whole text. A recap can also come in the middle of a text, after a long explanation, and it condenses what you just said into one short sentence. *En pocas palabras* ("in a few words") and *resumiendo* ("to sum up", the gerund of *resumir*) are made for that. They promise something shorter than what came before, so the sentence after them is short and clear.

sections.title: Long explanation, short recap
rows: La oficina abre a las nueve, cierra a las cinco y no abre los fines de semana. En pocas palabras, solo abre de lunes a viernes.
The office opens at nine, closes at five and does not open at weekends. In a few words, it only opens from Monday to Friday.
Resumiendo, el plan es barato, rápido y fácil.
To sum up, the plan is cheap, quick and easy.
En definitiva, es una buena idea.
All in all, it is a good idea.

sections.content: A restatement (*es decir*, *en otras palabras*) says the same thing in other words. A recap (*en pocas palabras*, *resumiendo*) gathers several things into one. If you have not said several things yet, there is nothing to recap.
